introduction.text: The Mitreo Barberini is one of the best preserved Mithraic temples in Rome, located behind Palazzo Barberini. It provides valuable insight into the early Roman mystery cult of Mithraism.

history.description: The western part of the building was converted into a Mithraeum in the 3rd century.
The site was excavated in 1936, revealing the remains of a 2nd-century building.

design.description: The Mithraeum is an 11.85 × 6.25 m vaulted hall with two benches on either side where participants lay during rites.

art.description: The central wall painting depicts the tauroctonia, with Mitra killing a bull, accompanied by Cautes, Cautopates, a dog, a serpent, and a scorpion, and zodiacal symbols above.
